subject.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings

question: Which Feishu bind grammar should OpenClaw support for conversation IDs while preserving existing account-scoped `--bind <channel>:<account>` behavior?
rationale: The PR fixes a real routing bug but changes a documented CLI grammar that writes persisted bindings; automation cannot safely choose between explicit peer syntax, Feishu-specific inference, or an account escape without maintainer product direction.

options.title: Preserve account syntax and add explicit peer routing
options.body: Keep `feishu:<account>` as account binding and add a documented peer/conversation form or plugin-owned resolver with compatibility tests.

options.title: Accept Feishu two-segment peer inference
options.body: Adopt `feishu:<id>` as peer inference only with an explicit account escape, docs, upgrade notes, and proof that account-scoped setups remain expressible.

options.title: Pause this branch and choose another candidate
options.body: Close or pause this PR if another open candidate better preserves compatibility and can supply stronger proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve account syntax and add explicit peer routing
recommendation.body: Keep `feishu:<account>` as account binding and add a documented peer/conversation form or plugin-owned resolver with compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the account-scoped bind and routing command contract this PR changes.
